text: Another often-proposed assumption is that Type II fibers are primarily responsible for exercise-induced increases in muscle size. This is principally based on studies showing that Type II fibers experience superior growth compared to Type I fibers after regimented resistance training (1, 40, 43, 1 1 1, 201, 217). When considered as a whole, the literature indicates that the growth capacity of Type II fibers is approximately 50% greater than that of Type I fibers (6), although substantial interindividual variability is seen in the extent of fiber type-specific hypertrophic adaptation (111). There also is evidence that the rate of muscle protein synthesis is elevated to a greater extent in the primarily fast-twitch human vastus lateralis muscle (approximately 50% to 60% Type II fibers)
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 1: Hypertrophy-Related Responses and Adaptations to Exercise Stress
